The number of solutions is p(7) = 15, the number of partitions of 7. The argument is a bijection with partitions.

Let s_i = b_1 + ... + b_i. Since every b_i is a positive integer, the s_i are strictly increasing positive integers, and the b_i are recovered uniquely from them. So a solution is the same as a choice of k, strictly increasing positive integers s_1 < ... < s_k, and positive integers a_i, satisfying

a_1 s_1 + a_2 s_2 + ... + a_k s_k = 7.

Read this as a partition of 7 in which the part s_i appears a_i times. The s_i are the distinct part sizes and the a_i are their multiplicities, both listed in increasing order of size. Every partition of 7 arises from exactly one such data set, and every data set gives a partition of 7. This is a bijection between solutions and partitions of 7.

The number of partitions of 7 is p(7) = 15.

ANSWER: 15
